chunks: 1755 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:

“Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves something for Himself and dislikes it for His creation. He, Mighty and Glorious, has disliked for His creation asking, and He has loved for Himself that He be asked. There is nothing more beloved to Him than that He be asked. So none of you should feel shy to ask Allah, Mighty and Glorious, from His bounty, even if it be the strap of a sandal.”

key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَةَ: asking, especially asking from created beings
key_terms.شِسْعَ نَعْلٍ: the strap of a sandal; a metaphor for even a very small need
key_terms.فَضْلِهِ: His bounty, grace, and generous provision
key_terms.يُسْأَلَ: to be asked; Allah loves that servants ask Him

ai.seo_question: Why should a believer ask Allah for even the smallest need?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that asking from people is disliked, while asking Allah is beloved to Him. It encourages believers to turn to Allah in du'a for all needs, even the smallest ones, and not to feel ashamed in seeking His bounty.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1755 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, loves something for Himself and dislikes it for His creation. He dislikes for His creation the act of asking [from others] but loves for Himself to be asked. There is nothing dearer to Him than being asked. So, let none of you feel shy to ask Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, for His bounty, even if it is [as small as] the strap of a sandal."
